messages.subject: Too much binning?
parts:
Sorry for the flurry of questions but I just wanted some input on this...I have applied binning and truncation to my data and I feel like I may have gone a bit overboard with trying to achieve a low as possible AIC on my model...attached is the plot of my half-normal detection function after truncating off at 99 and binning into the following cuts 0,49,51,80,99...is this model acceptable? I feel like it is a bit too manipulated and doesn't even resemble what a detection function should look like.

Thanks 

Steve

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: RE: [distance-sampling] Too much binning?
parts:
You cannot use AIC to select cutpoints.  AIC values can only be compared when models are fitted to the same data, and by binning the data in different ways, they are not the same.

 

You have rounding to 50m, so you need to choose cutpoints that avoid 50m – i.e. choose cutpoints so that any distance recorded as 50m is probably in the correct distance interval.  E.g. if you have a lot of rounding to the nearest 10m (but not to the nearest 5), you might select interval cutpoints of 0, 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, …

 

Steve Buckland
